environment.note: This is a distro-availability / feature-presence check, not a timing benchmark. Each query is a version string or a file-presence boolean, so it is deterministic and hardware-independent; CPU/GPU/RAM are intentionally omitted.

subject.name: systemd
subject.note: Upstream tag v261 (codename Edinburgh). The probes measure how far this release has propagated into distro container images.

baseline.name: distro-packaged systemd
baseline.note: The gap between upstream v261 and what each distro packages TODAY (Arch rolling vs Fedora/Debian/Ubuntu stable) is the finding. Compared by packaged version, not by measured timing.

image_pin_caveat: Images were pulled at :latest / :24.04 / :trixie-slim on 2026-07-24. These tags are mutable — re-running later will pull whatever those distros ship at that time, which is exactly the drift the probe measures. The committed probe-*-result.json is the 2026-07-24 snapshot.

measurement_bias_correction.note: probe.sh asked `systemctl --version` inside minimal base images. fedora/ubuntu/debian minimal images do not INSTALL systemd, so systemctl was absent — that says nothing about the packaged version. probe-pkg.sh corrects this by asking each distro's package manager directly (pacman/dnf/apt) what systemd version it packages right now.

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: none discarded — all evidence for this run is small and committed
raw_artifacts.note: Deterministic evidence (version strings + binary-presence booleans) lives in probe-result.json and probe-pkg-result.json. No large raw artifacts are produced. The four container images pulled to run the probes were removed after the run (received_images), per ownership-based cleanup; run.sh re-pulls them.
